items.question: On Hive mainnet I call chain.createTransaction(), push operations, and sign the transaction only 5 minutes later without having serialized it in between. Has the default expiration already passed, and when exactly is the default '+1m' resolved?
items.expected: No. The default '+1m' is applied lazily by flushTransaction() at the first flush (first serialize, sigDigest, id or signing) and only once, so an unflushed transaction does not consume its window; the first flush fixes expiration = local realtime + 1 minute on mainnet. After that first flush the value is locked, so a preview or log that serializes the transaction early does start the window. (On non-mainnet chain ids the reference is the head block time captured at createTransaction.)
forbidden: expiration is fixed at createTransaction() time
expiration is recomputed on every serialize or sign
on mainnet wax takes the expiration reference from the API node's head block time

items.question: Does tx.validate() in wax confirm that the accounts named in my operations exist on chain and that my signatures satisfy their authorities?
items.expected: No. validate() calls cpp_tx_validate, an offline structural/protocol check with no API access. Chain-state checks belong to the OnlineTransaction returned by chain.createTransaction(): its async validate(operations) hooks resolve accounts through the API and performOnChainVerification() runs recursive, API-backed authority verification, which chain.broadcast(tx) invokes before network_broadcast_api.broadcast_transaction when the transaction is an OnlineTransaction.
forbidden: validate() queries the node to check that accounts exist
validate() verifies the signatures against on-chain authorities
broadcast performs no authority pre-check of any kind
items.applies: wax 2.0.2 (TS); Python 2.0.1 has the same Transaction / OnlineTransaction split

items.question: How many operations does wax's protobuf operation oneof define, how many of them can be pushed into a transaction, and which hive-core regular operations are missing from wax?

items.question: A Node.js service keeps a single createHiveChain() instance alive for weeks; after some days every wax call throws RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds (or unreachable). Will wax recover by itself, and what should the service do?
items.expected: No. WasmManager caches the Emscripten module in mainModule and never resets it, and safeWasmCall only translates thrown C++ exceptions into typed Wax* errors (unrecognized ones become a generic WaxError), so a corrupted module stays poisoned for the process lifetime. The service must detect the WASM runtime error itself, drop its cached chain/foundation object and rebuild it (each createHiveChain / createWaxFoundation call constructs a new WasmManager and loads the module afresh), which is how consumers such as denser handle it.
forbidden: wax automatically reloads the WASM module after a RuntimeError
retrying the same call on the same instance will eventually succeed
this is a hived node problem, so switch the API endpoint
